name: Pomelo
imageAlt: large ripe pale green and yellow pomelo cut in half, revealing thick rind and dense segments of translucent tear-shaped pulpy vesicles
description: The pomelo (Citrus maximus) is the principal ancestral citrus species, housing a dense cellular structure engineered for targeted vascular regulation, profound collagen synthesis, and systemic lymphatic drainage. The primary therapeutic blueprint of the pomelo lies in its exceptional yield of L-ascorbic acid, working alongside unique flavanone glycosides—principally naringenin and neohesperidin—and high molecular weight soluble pectins. Operating within human biochemical environments, these compounds enhance white blood cell kinetics, sweep away circulating low-density lipoproteins, and strengthen the delicate micro-vascular endothelium.
macroIntro: Pomelo delivers an ultra-hydrating, hypocaloric macro profile characterized by high water density and a light structural fiber network.
microIntro: The crisp, translucent vesicles isolate a massive reservoir of antioxidant ascorbic acid, cell-protecting bioflavonoids, and dynamic fluid-regulating electrolytes.

healthBenefits: Immune System Amplification: Massive native Vitamin C parameters maximize white blood cell mobilization, accelerating defensive responses against external viral pathogens.
Cardiovascular Lipid Management: Active naringenin and soluble citrus fibers work to inhibit hepatic cholesterol synthesis, protecting arterial walls from plaque deposition.
Vascular Pressure Stabilization: High intracellular potassium ratios actively drop smooth muscle vascular tone, supporting balanced systemic blood pressure loops.
Dermal Collagen Assembly: The synergy of ascorbic acid and bioflavonoids directly catalyzes the hydroxylation of proline, upgrading skin elasticity and tissue repair.
Metabolic Optimization: The distinct, low-calorie, enzyme-rich pulp structure assists in modulating postprandial glucose curves, supporting healthy weight management profiles.
precautionsIntro: Cytochrome P450 Drug-Interactions, Gastrointestinal Organic Acid Stress, and Citric Hyper-Sensitivities: Clinical awareness ensures safe inclusion.
precautions: Cytochrome P450 Enzyme Inhibition (Furanocoumarins): Like grapefruit, pomelo contains furanocoumarins that inhibit the intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme system. This can unsafely raise blood concentrations of specific medications—such as statins, calcium channel blockers, and immunosuppressants—triggering toxic complications.

Gastrointestinal Mucosal Irritation: The raw pulp possesses concentrated natural citric acid. Individuals suffering from acute gastritis, active peptic ulcer disease, or severe gastroesophageal reflux (GERD) may experience burning pain and acid regurgitation due to direct mucosal irritation.

True Citrus Sensitivity and Contact Dermatitis: Pomelo contains highly reactive essential oils (like limonene) in its thick rind and specific proteins in its pulp. Hyper-sensitive individuals can experience localized allergic reactions, including oral tingling, lip swelling, or contact dermatitis from handling the outer peel.
